top_stories.title: Malware Can Abuse Windows Hello for Business Keys for Persistent Entra ID Access
top_stories.summary: Researcher Dirk-jan Mollema demonstrated that malware executing within a signed-in Windows session can silently leverage Windows Hello for Business keys to authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID without user interaction. The attack enables persistent cloud access by allowing the attacker to register a controlled device, obtain a Primary Refresh Token (PRT), and add additional authentication methods depending on tenant policies.

top_stories.title: Hackers Impersonate IT Support to Breach Leading Financial Companies
top_stories.summary: A hacking campaign operating under names including Redact, Pink, Falcon, and Helix impersonated IT help desks to steal MFA credentials from employees at over 200 financial firms. The attackers built fake credential-stealing websites to capture authentication data from targeted employees.

top_stories.title: Azure DevOps service connections now replace PATs across pipeline tasks
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has updated Azure DevOps pipelines to support authentication via Microsoft Entra service principals or managed identities, replacing Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and build session tokens. The new Azure DevOps service connection supports cross-organization repository access, representing a shift toward more secure, token-free authentication in CI/CD pipelines.

top_stories.title: 200 accounts compromised in Swiss government’s Microsoft SharePoint breach
top_stories.summary: Hackers exploited Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities in Switzerland's Federal Office of Information Technology, Systems and Telecommunication (BIT), compromising login credentials for approximately 200 accounts. BIT detected unusual activity on July 28, blocked internet access to the platform, closed the exploited vulnerabilities, and confirmed credential theft on July 31.

top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 AitM Phishing Hijacks Accounts to Collect Payroll and Finance Emails
top_stories.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified an active phishing campaign using adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) techniques to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts and target financial personnel. The attack uses residential proxies to bypass detection and focuses on harvesting payroll and finance-related emails from compromised accounts.

news.title: Atlassian Rovo Can Be Tricked Into Sending Jira and Confluence Data to Attackers
news.summary: Security researchers found that Atlassian's Rovo AI assistant can be manipulated via prompt injection to exfiltrate Jira and Confluence data accessible to a signed-in user. Two security firms independently discovered the vulnerability through different attack routes, with only one confirmed as patched.

news.title: New CSS Attacks Can Break Webmail Defenses to Steal Passwords and Tokens
news.summary: New research by PortSwigger's Gareth Heyes demonstrates CSS-based attacks that allow malicious email content to escape message boundaries and interfere with webmail interfaces across Outlook, Gmail, Fastmail, Proton Mail, Yahoo Mail, and AOL Mail. The attack chains can capture passwords, leak authentication tokens, hijack UI actions, and take over third-party accounts.

news.title: Interview: SailPoint says Taiwan hardware leads but identity governance lags
news.summary: SailPoint's managing director for Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau stated that Taiwan's hardware manufacturing sector leads globally but its investment in cybersecurity software and identity governance lags behind the Asia-Pacific region. The interview highlights a regional gap in identity governance adoption despite Taiwan's strong technology manufacturing presence.

news.title: How Okta, IBD Stock Of The Day, Is Targeting 'Nonhuman' Identity Opportunity
news.summary: Okta is targeting the emerging "nonhuman" identity market as AI-based agents performing internet tasks require new identity and access management safeguards. Okta stock has surged over 70% in 2026, driven by investor interest in the company's positioning around AI agent identity security.

news.title: A decade of enterprise identity in the cloud with AWS Managed Microsoft AD
news.summary: AWS is marking the 10-year anniversary of AWS Managed Microsoft AD (AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory), its fully managed Active Directory service in the cloud. The article reviews the service's evolution over the decade, covering enterprise identity management capabilities delivered through a managed AD infrastructure on AWS.

news.title: Show HN: I scanned 30 production MCP servers' OAuth – only 1 earned an A
news.summary: A developer released an open-source scanner that tested OAuth conformance across 30 production MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, with only one achieving an "A" grade. The tool implements IETF draft specifications for OAuth identity chaining and transaction tokens, available as a CLI, GitHub Action, and hosted scanner.

news.title: What's new with SAML support in Nextcloud
news.summary: Nextcloud has updated its user_saml application, which enables single sign-on via SAML and Kerberos protocols. The post is written by a Nextcloud developer who recently joined the IdP team and now co-maintains the application.

news.title: Swiss government SharePoint breach compromised 200 accounts
news.summary: Swiss federal IT office confirmed hackers exploited vulnerabilities in Microsoft SharePoint servers, compromising approximately 200 government accounts. The breach targeted Switzerland's federal IT infrastructure, resulting in unauthorized access to a significant number of government user accounts.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian cybercriminal Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges related to hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data storage platform. The attacks involved credential-based intrusions targeting Snowflake customer accounts, resulting in the theft of over 100 million AT&T customer records.

news.title: Microsoft Teams PowerShell 7.9: WAM authentication and administrator changes
news.summary: Microsoft Teams PowerShell module 7.9.0 introduces Web Account Manager (WAM) as the authentication broker for interactive Windows sign-ins. The release also includes new commands and policy parameters alongside the authentication change.

news.title: Securing AI agents with temporal policies in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore introduces temporal policies that enable stateful, session-history-based authorization rules for AI agents. The feature supports workflow sequencing enforcement, financial exposure caps, and human approval requirements for agentic AI systems.

news.title: Discounted Claude access bought on the gray market may expose every prompt you send
news.summary: Okta discovered more than half a dozen gray market services on underground forums offering discounted or unlimited access to frontier AI models like Claude. The investigation was conducted by Okta's threat intelligence team, making it an Okta research finding rather than a core IAM topic.

news.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
news.summary: Device code phishing attacks have increased 1,500% in 2026, with vishing attacks doubling over the same period. These social engineering techniques bypass traditional authentication controls by exploiting legitimate OAuth device code flows, directly undermining MFA and authentication security measures.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA issued a postmortem report on a data leak where a contractor exposed dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management failures and gaps in secrets detection, with the breach only identified after KrebsOnSecurity notified the agency.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping and MFA bypass techniques used to compromise major organizations.
